llm.reply:
Lynch syndrome has retrieved records in this system spanning associated genes, the disease record, and clinical studies. The gene set centres on DNA mismatch repair genes. One linked gene is NCBIGene:4292, mutL homolog 1 [10].

## Mismatch Repair Genes

Another linked gene is NCBIGene:4436, mutS homolog 2 [11]. The set also includes NCBIGene:2956, mutS homolog 6 [8]. NCBIGene:5395 is PMS1 homolog 2, mismatch repair system component [14]. NCBIGene:5378 is PMS1 homolog 1, mismatch repair system component [13]. NCBIGene:27030 is mutL homolog 3 [6].

## Other Associated Genes

The records also link genes outside mismatch repair. These include NCBIGene:4072, epithelial cell adhesion molecule [9]. Others are NCBIGene:7048, transforming growth factor beta receptor 2 [16], NCBIGene:999, cadherin 1 [17], NCBIGene:4763, neurofibromin 1 [12], and NCBIGene:6224, ribosomal protein S20 [15].

## Condition and Trials

The disease record is named Lynch syndrome [7]. One study is Implementation of a New Strategy to Identify HNPCC Patients [1]. Another is Registry for Women Who Are At Risk Or May Have Lynch Syndrome [5]. A further study is Psychosocial Aspects of Genetic Testing for Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colon Cancer [3].

## Supporting Literature

The MedGen concept is titled Lynch syndrome [19]. Related literature includes Differentiating Lynch-like from Lynch syndrome. [22]. Another review is Lynch Syndrome Genetics and Clinical Implications. [30].

Retrieval links Lynch syndrome to a set of genes centred on DNA mismatch repair, and to several registered clinical studies. ## Clinical Studies

One trial is Implementation of a New Strategy to Identify HNPCC Patients [1]. Another is Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer in Taiwan-Related Genetic Study and Clinical Applications [2]. Another is Psychosocial Aspects of Genetic Testing for Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colon Cancer [3]. Another is Educational CD-ROM Compared With Standard Informed Consent for Patients With Colorectal Cancer or a Family History of Colorectal Cancer [4].
